prompt_text: What is the best health insurance broker in Kansas City MO for someone who is self-employed?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” broker for everyone — the right broker depends on your exact needs (which state — MO or KS side of Kansas City? — your budget, whether you want ACA marketplace plans, an HSA-friendly plan, dental/vision, or association/small‑group options). That said, for a self‑employed person you’ll generally get the best outcome from an independent, licensed broker who:

- Specializes in individual/sole‑proprietor and ACA marketplace plans
- Can shop multiple carriers (not captive to one insurer)
- Understands Missouri/Kansas rules and subsidy eligibility through HealthCare.gov
- Will run plan comparisons using your estimated income and health needs
- Is available year‑round for questions (not just during open enrollment)

Where to look and how to pick
1. Start with the federal marketplace (HealthCare.gov) — you may qualify for premium tax credits. Brokers and certified navigators can help you enroll through the marketplace.
2. Search for local independent insurance brokers or “ACA navigators” in Kansas City. Independent brokers give access to more carriers than captive agents.
3. Vet brokers:
   - Verify license with the Missouri Department of Commerce & Insurance (or Kansas Insurance Department if you’re on the KS side).
   - Ask whether they charge you a fee (many are paid by carriers; some charge a client fee).
   - Ask how many individual clients they serve, what carriers they work with, whether they help with subsidy calculations, and whether they provide year‑round service.
   - Request references or read Google/Yelp reviews.
4. Ask specific questions:
   - “Can you compare total yearly cost for these plans using my expected income and medical use?”
   - “Do you help with Marketplace enrollment, special enrollment periods, and ACA appeals?”
   - “Are you independent, and which carriers do you represent?”
   - “Is there a client fee or commission I should know about?”

Channels that work well for self‑employed people
- Certified navigators (for subsidy help on HealthCare.gov)
- Independent local brokers who work ACA + off‑exchange plans
- Reputable online marketplaces (eHealth, HealthSherpa) if you prefer a mostly self‑service approach

If you want, I can:
- Find specific, highly rated independent brokers or navigator organizations in Kansas City if you share your zip code and whether you’re in Missouri or Kansas
- Prepare a short list of questions to email/ask brokers when you contact them

Which would you prefer?
